newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shokusan to open special accounts for shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Shokusan to open special accounts for shareholders.

text.p: Shokusan Bank, a regional bank mainly operating in Yamagata Prefecture in northern Japan, said on Tuesday it would open special deposit accounts for its shareholders with a higher interest rate than for other customers.
The accounts are to celebrate the bank's listing on the second section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange last month.
The deposits will mature in one year, and the interest rate will be 0.5 percentage point higher than the bank's usual rate on one-year deposits.
Holders of 1,000 or more shares as of March 31, 1997, will be able to submit applications to open the accounts between June 16 and August 29, the bank said.
